title: The pebble's circles
intro: In the story a pebble drops into the water and makes circles that spread out. At home a bowl of water is enough to see them for real: the activity is done without the tablet.

3-5.goal: Look and listen to what a pebble does when it falls into the water.
steps: The child drops one pebble at a time into the bowl, gently.
Each of you says what you see (the circles) and what you hear (plink).
When the water is still again, try another pebble.
materials: a large bowl with a little water
two or three smooth pebbles, bigger than a walnut
a tea towel to dry up
preparation: Put the bowl on a low table or on the floor, on top of the tea towel.
Put the pebbles on a small plate next to the bowl.

supervision.note: Small pebbles can end up in a mouth: pick big ones and stay next to the child for the whole game.

alternatives: Without pebbles: leaves or big bottle caps to drop.
Outside: a puddle or a fountain, holding the child's hand.

6-7.goal: Discover that different stones make different circles.
steps: The child picks three stones of different sizes and lines them up, smallest to biggest.
Says out loud which one will make the biggest circles.
Drops them one at a time, watches and checks whether the guess was right.
Puts the stones back and dries up any spilled water.
materials: a bowl or basin with water
preparation: Gather the stones, bowl and cloth together on a surface that can get wet.
Let the child choose the stones.

supervision.note: It is enough for you to be in the room and for the stones to be too big to go in a mouth. No need to say whether the guess was right: looking together is enough.

alternatives: Use the sink with a little water if you have no bowl.
Use three balls of different weights instead of stones.

8-10.goal: Run a test, see what happens and tell about it.
steps: The child decides what to find out (for example: do the circles change if the stone falls from higher up?).
Draws the plan: what will be used and in what order.
Does the test and notes or draws what happens.
Tells out loud what changed compared to the plan, and why.
materials: stones or other small things that sink
preparation: Leave the materials in a corner where it is fine to get wet.
Just say there is a test to do: the child chooses the question.

supervision.note: The child can do it all alone; just ask to be told about it afterwards. Stay close if using a full sink or if outdoors.

alternatives: Use a puddle or a fountain if you pass one during the day.
Use a magnifying glass to look closely at the circles, if the child asks for it.
